deck_title: Doppler-Fizeau moving-source bow compression vs naive rigid bullseye wave rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Christian Doppler (1842) & Hippolyte Fizeau (1848) moving-source retarded wavefront compression law (lambda_front = lambda_0*(1 - M) where Mach ratio M = v_s/c = u/(1+u) in [0.0000, 0.5000], compressing forward bow-wave crest spacing as the emitter chases its own wave crests so lambda_model/lambda_exact locks at 1.0000x across all 17 stations with 0/17 uncompressed stations) versus naive rigidly translated bullseye waves (sin(k_0*|x - x_s(t)| - omega_0*t), which ignores retarded emission positions x_s(t - tau) and leaves forward wavelength uncompressed at lambda_0, overestimating bow-wave spacing by 1/(1 - M) = 1 + u up to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at M=0.50 u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-step Lienard-Wiechert retarded-time iteration.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Moving water-skimmer ripples, swimming waterfowl wakes, sub-sonic acoustic shock rings, and moving radar/sonar pulse visualizations
Compressing forward wave crests by (1 - M*cos(theta)) and stretching trailing stern crests by (1 + M*cos(theta))
Eliminating the rigid-plastic-bullseye artifact when a ripple emitter translates across a water surface
Closed-form directional Doppler wavenumber k(theta) = k_0 / (1 - M * dot(v_hat, r_hat))
not_for: Strictly stationary buoys or fountains with zero horizontal translation velocity (M = 0)
